25 A source emits a progressive sound wave in the horizontal direction. The wave travels away from
the source in a direction towards the right.
The graph shows the variation of the displacement of the particles from their equilibrium positions
with distance from the source at a particular instant in time. Displacements to the right of the
equilibrium positions are shown as positive.
displacement

Position Y represents the displacement of a particle in the sound wave at a particular distance
from the source at this instant.
Which statement about the motion of this particle is correct?
A
The particle is moving away from the source.
B
The particle is moving towards the source.
C
The particle is moving upwards.
D
The particle is moving downwards.

hints: Notice Y is on the right-hand rising slope of the displacement-distance graph where displacement is negative and increasing with distance.
Recall the whole longitudinal profile travels to the right, so after a short time the displacement at the fixed position of Y is replaced by the displacement that is currently just to its left.
Compare the displacement just to the left of Y, nearer the trough, with the displacement at Y to decide whether the particle must move left or right next.
walkthrough: Identify the given information: a longitudinal sound wave travels to the right, and the graph plots horizontal particle displacement $x$ against distance, with positive $x$ to the right.
State the governing idea: for a progressive wave the displacement-distance profile keeps its shape and shifts in the direction of wave travel, here to larger distance.
Look at position Y: it is at negative displacement on a slope that rises toward zero as distance increases, with the trough to its left.

Imagine a small time $\Delta t$ later: the profile has moved a small distance $v\Delta t$ to the right, so the particle fixed at Y now has the displacement previously held by the point just to its left.
The point just to the left of Y is closer to the trough and more negative than Y, so the displacement at Y decreases and becomes more negative.
More negative means a shift to the left, which is back towards the source on the left. This is option B.

A.explanation: Moving away from the source means moving to the right, but the wave profile shifting right makes the displacement at Y more negative.

B.explanation: The wave profile moves right, so Y takes on the more negative displacement from just to its left and therefore moves left towards the source.

C.explanation: Sound is a longitudinal wave so particles oscillate horizontally along the wave direction, not vertically upwards.

D.explanation: Sound is a longitudinal wave so particles oscillate horizontally along the wave direction, not vertically downwards.
